correctness.rationale: For M_n, each extensive isotone idempotent endomap has one of the unique forms A_S, B_i, or C, determined by its image of 0. The A maps compose by intersection; B_i B_j=C for i≠j; C absorbs all maps; and A_S and B_i commute exactly for i in S. These identities yield all maximal families F_J. Inclusion-exclusion on exactly occurring B_i gives the ordered k-tuple formula and exponential generating function. Enumeration of small labelled diamonds corroborates the general elementary proof; finite tests alone do not establish it.

originality.rationale: Glück has already established the individual closure-map classification and 2^n+n+1 diamond count; neither is claimed as new. The additional commutation criterion, 2^n maximal commuting families, their sizes, and all-arity tuple enumeration are not consequences of that unrefined count. The inspected general monotone-operator fixed-point work assumes commuting operators without classifying which pairs commute. The modal-multilattice logic paper concerns a different algebraic semantics. This is a qualified best-of-knowledge comparison, not a priority certification.
residual_risks: An unindexed finite semigroup or idempotent-transformation theorem may contain an equivalent commutation graph classification.
The 2022 modal-multilattice full text was not obtained; its different focus is supported only by accessible abstract, not whole-paper review.
Search failures do not establish exhaustive priority; Lemma numbering in Glück differs among versions.

value.rationale: Commutation is the exact condition for order-independent composition of extensive isotone idempotent modalities. On the smallest natural nondistributive atom diamonds, the result classifies all maximal compatible families and counts arbitrary ordered commuting tuples with repetition. These are exact structural invariants of a natural infinite-parameter model, not arbitrary finite-case enumeration; scope is deliberately restricted to this lattice family.
